locked_build: Arrival Notice Desk, deterministic workflow with one conditional extraction node, Bethel

ASK_RESIZED.what_happened: The roi-analyst built the case for the six-week desk as briefed and reported honestly that its CONSERVATIVE case does not clear. Computed in code: 57 percent of five-year TCO recovered, no payback inside the horizon. Under the ROI_METHOD decision rule the ask shrinks until its conservative case stands on its own, so the showrunner resized it.
ASK_RESIZED.new_ask: A two-week format-and-contact-data finding at Bethel. The deliverable IS the decision.
ASK_RESIZED.why_it_clears: Conservative recovers 217 percent of TCO with payback at month 28, and it clears on a CASH line alone with zero capacity dollars in the formula. All three scenarios pay back inside the horizon.
ASK_RESIZED.the_desk_is_what_the_finding_gates: The six-week desk is not dropped. It is what the finding decides, and it gets approved with MEASURED drivers replacing assumed ones, not before.

staff_engineer.one_liner: A desk that turns the daily on-hand count Bethel already runs into a written, timestamped arrival notice per consignee, released by the agent who handled the freight that day, so freight leaves the floor sooner and the storage clause in Ryan Air's own tariff finally has the written record it depends on.

nodes.label: Sheet reader, only if no export

architecture.caption: Two possible ways in, and we expect only one of them gets built. If the daily on-hand list comes out of Takeflite as an export or a spreadsheet, the sheet reader is deleted from scope and no model touches any part of this. The reader is drawn plain rather than as part of the build for that reason. Nothing reaches a consignee until a Bethel agent releases the batch, and every released notice is written to our own log with its send timestamp, which is the record the storage clause rests on. We hold no Takeflite credentials and write nothing back to it.

staff_engineer.build_vs_buy_summary: BUY FIRST, before anyone is paid: ask whether Takeflite already offers freight arrival notification, and whether Saltchuk shared services owns this, since sibling Northern Air Cargo already ships a self-serve estimator. BUY the sheet reader (Document AI or Textract, per page) only if the reconciliation is paper, and it is deleted entirely on an export. BUY managed Postgres, a small app host, Postmark for email, Twilio for text, OIDC sign-in, Sentry. BUILD only the parts that encode Ryan Air's own rules: the arrival diff, the storage clock calculator (their published three-day rule as a pure function over an Anchorage station calendar), the consignee matcher POLICY (bought algorithm, built thresholds and queue), the fixed notice template, the release screen, and the append-only notice ledger whose shape IS the product because it is the evidentiary artifact the tariff depends on.

cross_cutting.auth: Three roles, station agent, station lead, admin. Scoping enforced by row-level security in Postgres, not by hiding buttons, so an interface mistake can't leak another station's freight. The row-level policy partitions by CARRIER as well as station, which is the Everts rule in code. We hold NO Takeflite credential of any kind, deliberately, so no part of this design can be blocked by a third party saying no.
cross_cutting.data_security: Consignee names and shipment references are identifying data in a village of a few hundred people, so this is sensitive from day one. The notice carries the shipment reference, arrival timestamp, station and the date fees would begin, and nothing else. No commodity description, no weight, no shipper name, no contents, because a notice read over someone's shoulder at a village counter should reveal nothing about what is in the box. Raw reconciliation files deleted 30 days after reconcile, notice records retained 18 months. A bounced address is NEVER retried against a guessed alternative, since guessing an address in a small community is how a private shipment reaches the wrong household. Notices go to one consignee at a time, never a group.
cross_cutting.observability: Four live numbers visible to the station lead from day one. OVERRIDE RATE, the rubber-stamp detector, alarming in BOTH directions, above 20 percent means the diff is wrong and at zero over five consecutive days means the review became theatre. SUPPRESSION RATE, the honest measure of how much still needs a person. BOUNCE AND FAILURE RATE, because an undelivered notice is not a notice. TIME FROM NOTICE TO COLLECTION, the number that says whether any of this moved freight.
cross_cutting.failure_modes: The safe state is silence and every failure path routes to it. No file by cutoff, the desk does not run and alerts the lead. Columns changed, the schema check fails and the ENTIRE batch is suppressed rather than partially processed. Carrier column missing where Everts freight can sit on the same floor, that station is blocked. Below threshold or any first-time consignee, queued and never sent, no exceptions. Bounce or text failure, undelivered means NEVER NOTIFIED, so the storage clock never starts on it. A wrong notice already sent, one button sends the correction, voids the original and sets fee_eligible false permanently. The desk down, Bethel works exactly as it does today. There is no degraded mode that sends without a person and there never will be.

staff_engineer.riskiest_assumption: That the consignee side of a Bethel airbill carries a written channel Ryan Air can actually reach, an email address or a mobile that takes text, for enough shipments that a written-notice desk changes anything. Everything else in this design has a fallback. This one has none. If most village consignees are reachable only by a call to a village agent or a sheet posted at the counter, the send leg is aimed at a channel that does not exist and phase one is contact capture, a data project wearing none of this architecture. All eight stations publishing a fax number is a hint that today's written notification may be paper, and a hint is not a finding.
staff_engineer.spike: Two weeks, fixed fee, at Bethel, no production code. Days 1-2, take ten consecutive days of the daily on-hand reconciliation exactly as the station produces it and answer four things: export or sheet, does it carry a carrier column, is the shipment reference stable day to day, does anyone keep yesterday's copy. Days 3-6, pull 200 consecutive airbills for freight that landed at Bethel and count what contact channel each one actually carries, which produces the one number this whole design rests on. Count how many arrival notices go out today and by what means. Days 7-8, sit at the counter for two shifts and count and time arrival-status calls. Days 9-10, write it up as a go or no-go with THREE DOORS. Door A, export exists and contacts are there, build the desk with no model in it and say so loudly. Door B, export exists and contacts are not, phase one is contact capture and the desk ships behind it. Door C, paper only, price the reader against real sheets scored on a human-transcribed set, or walk away. No extraction accuracy figure may be spoken aloud before those sheets are in hand.

delivery.walking_skeleton: One shipment for one consignee, end to end, hard parts on crutches. A CSV placed by hand, one consignee typed in, the diff against an empty prior snapshot, the REAL storage clock calculator, the REAL template, the REAL release screen with one line, Postmark in test mode to a Ryan Air inbox, and one genuine ledger row carrying the provider send timestamp. If the ledger row is wrong at this size it is wrong at every size, so it gets found in week one for the price of a day.
delivery.then: Ten days of real files through a real schema check, the directory seeded from airbills, the matcher threshold tuned against real village names, the carrier partition in the database, the retraction path, the day-two reminder, bounce webhooks, real roles, four live metrics. Then TWO WEEKS OF SHADOW RUNNING where the desk produces and the agent reviews the full daily batch and NOTHING SENDS, so Bethel sees exactly what the desk would have told its customers before it tells them anything. The override rate from that fortnight is the acceptance evidence. Only then does the button send for real.
delivery.estimate_range: Spike 2 to 3 weeks, high confidence, ~80 percent. Door A 5 to 8 weeks to a live desk including shadow, moderate confidence ~60 percent. Door B adds 4 to 10 weeks of counter capture, low confidence ~40 percent, because the pace is set by shipment turnover rather than by us. Door C adds 3 to 6 weeks plus per-page vendor cost, low confidence ~35 percent. Honest whole-project span 6 to 20 weeks depending which door opens, and that width is real rather than padding. The Cone of Uncertainty narrows when decisions get made, and two of ours are already made, one station and one daily trigger.

product_manager.problem: Ryan Air's own tariff makes this a billing question, not a courtesy one. The freight rules page says storage fees may be applied for shipments held more than three days after WRITTEN NOTIFICATION of arrival at the destination point, at $.75 per 100 pounds or part thereof per day. The clock does not start when the freight lands. It starts when the consignee is told, in writing, that it landed. That one sentence turns a written arrival notice into a billing instrument at every station, and it means the fee they publish is only as solid as the record of the notice behind it. The raw material already exists, the Bethel Lead Cargo Agent posting says an on-hand reconciliation is completed daily and that all mail and freight received is input into TakeFlite. What can't be seen from outside is what happens next, whether every arriving airbill produces a written notice, how quickly, and where those notices are kept.
product_manager.reason_now: The Bethel CSA spec puts greeting and assisting customers with locating their freight over the counter and on the telephone on the same people, and four of the ten current open postings are at Bethel, so agent minutes at that station are the scarcest thing in the building. Meanwhile the expectation shippers arrive with has moved, Lynden pushes automated email at five milestones including when a shipment is available for pickup, at Bethel, Emmonak, Kotzebue, Nome and St. Mary's, five of Ryan Air's own stations.
product_manager.not_neglect: None of this reads as a company that stopped tending its rules. The freight rules page was updated in late July, days before we looked, and nine customer-facing pages changed in the last six weeks. This is the kind of gap a busy carrier carries while its rates team ships every month, which is also why it is cheap to close.

metrics.metric: Share of arriving freight shipments at Bethel receiving a timestamped written arrival notice within 24 hours of arrival.
metrics.baseline: UNKNOWN today and we will not guess it. Measured across two weeks of real arrivals from their own reconciliation sheets, written down and shown to them before any target is scored against it.
metrics.timeframe: First read at the end of the pilot, held and reported at two quarters from go-live. If the measured baseline turns out to already be near 90, we say so and the value shifts to the record and the two open questions.

metrics.metric: Station-agent minutes per week at Bethel on where-is-my-freight and has-it-landed contacts, counter and phone.
metrics.baseline: UNKNOWN, and it has to be MADE rather than sourced. We refuse to import another carrier's number and call it theirs. A two-week stopwatch tally before go-live, sampled the same way after so the comparison is like for like.
metrics.target: Down by a third against that measured tally
metrics.timeframe: Two quarters from go-live, first comparable four-week window read at the end of the pilot.

metrics.metric: Customer-facing statements of rate or policy that turn out to be wrong. HARD GUARDRAIL on both metrics above, not a nice-to-have.
metrics.baseline: Counted over the same two pre-go-live weeks from corrections, disputes and retractions the station knows about.
metrics.target: Zero increase over baseline. If agent minutes fall while wrong notices rise, the build failed whatever the first two numbers say, and that is the sentence that goes in the read-out.
metrics.timeframe: Reviewed weekly. Any wrong notice triaged within one business day and retracted through a path that ships in version one. No storage fee may ever be raised on a flagged, held, corrected or retracted line.

non_goals.item: No voice or chat agent, in phase one or as a phase two we are quietly holding back.
non_goals.reason: We killed it at our own feasibility gate and we would rather tell them that than sell it. Every question it would field decomposes into a lookup or arithmetic that ordinary software does at effectively 100 percent, testable and cheaper. All three of its likely jobs are money statements, a rate quote is six interacting modifiers, an arrival answer starts the storage clock, and a refund answer is a promise against a published ten business day window. Nobody reviews a live call while it is happening. In Moffatt v. Air Canada the tribunal held that a carrier is responsible for all the information on its website. With eight stations serving 70 to 80 villages under a tagline about serving friends and family for over 70 years, one bad interaction travels the whole community.

The notice starts a billable clock, so the person who physically handled that freight is the only reviewer holding real ground truth. Removing that step would not make the system better, it would remove the one control that makes it safe.

non_goals.item: No writes into Takeflite and no dependency on Takeflite API access in phase one.
non_goals.reason: Access is granted by the vendor, not by Ryan Air, and it is unverified today. Designing around it would put their delivery date inside somebody else's contract negotiation.

non_goals.item: No rate, tariff interpretation or policy written in free text by the system.
non_goals.reason: The notice carries the shipment reference, arrival timestamp and the storage start date computed from the rule they already publish. Anything beyond that links to their own page.

non_goals.item: No rollout to a second station in phase one, and no price quoted for one.
non_goals.reason: Two things that materially change the build are unknown and one can block it. Pricing a network rollout first would be reverse-engineering a number to clear an approval, and they would be holding the resulting estimate.

non_goals.item: Nothing in the dispatch, weather or flight-planning lane.
non_goals.reason: That work is real, MIT Lincoln Laboratory's visibility tool reads existing FAA camera feeds at more than 90 percent accuracy on low visibility. We still decline it, because the cost of an error there is a human life and the human relay is the safety control.

non_goals.item: No self-serve rate estimator or customer account portal in phase one.
non_goals.reason: Sibling Northern Air Cargo already runs a self-serve estimator across 16 cargo categories inside the same Saltchuk Aviation family. The cheapest path there is probably reuse, not a build from us. We would rather say that now than bill for it later.

non_goals.item: No build on the airbill tracker, including the missing Bypass Mail Order lookup.
non_goals.reason: Everts exposes a Bypass Mail Order number on the same Takeflite platform Ryan Air already pays for, so it may be a tenant setting rather than a build. Open a support ticket first. If it is a setting, nobody should be paid for it, us included.

need_from_you: Real on-hand reconciliation sheets from Bethel, the last 10 to 14 days, in whatever form they exist, including photographs of paper. This is the single input that decides whether this build contains a model at all, and we won't promise an extraction accuracy figure before holding real sheets.

A decision on consignee contact data. What current details exist, which system holds them, who owns them, and whether we may use them. If that data is not there, phase one becomes contact capture, a data project at a different shape and price. We would rather say that before anyone signs than discover it in week four.
A named owner at Bethel who reviews and releases the batch, roughly two hours a week during the pilot. Without a named person the pilot has no ground truth and the review becomes decoration.

Sign-off on exactly what the notice says, from whoever owns the tariff and rules language. This is a document with Ryan Air's name on it that starts a billable clock, so it goes out in words they approved rather than words we chose.
Two weeks of access to take the baselines before go-live.
A decision on the delivery channel and sending address.

Confirmation of who approves a one-hub pilot. Ryan Air is one of six Saltchuk Aviation companies and shared services could reasonably claim this work. We sized the ask to sit inside a single operating decision for exactly that reason, and we would rather learn in week one than at the approval.
open_questions: What form does the daily on-hand reconciliation at Bethel actually take? This decides whether the build contains any model at all, and we are hoping the answer is export.
Do current, usable contact details exist for the consignees on those sheets?
How does a station give written notification of arrival today, and where is it kept? Eight stations publishing a fax number is a hint, not an answer.
What exactly may the notice say, field by field, and who signs off that wording?
Can a one-hub pilot be approved as a Ryan Air operating decision, or does Saltchuk Aviation Shared Services need to see it first?

Does Takeflite already sell arrival notification for freight, and can the Bypass Mail Order number be enabled on the tracker as Everts exposes it? One support ticket, and we should not be paid for the answer.
Does the Bethel on-hand list distinguish carrier, and freight from bypass mail? This decides whether Aniak and Nome can ever run the same desk.
What is the freight cutoff time at Bethel, and is it the same at every station? Their rules page publishes none, and it is the one input a status message or an estimate can't be fully honest without.

roi_analyst.why_six_week_fails: With no volume baseline, the honest FLOOR on recurring recovered minutes is about the same size as the honest annual run cost, so the desk pays for itself only if the arrival-status load at Bethel is larger than that floor, which is exactly the thing nobody can see from outside.

benefit_lines.basis: ASSUMED throughout. Hours per operating day 1.0 / 2.0 / 3.5, fully loaded rate 26 / 30 / 34, cut 0.30 to 0.50 and never higher because the reviewer still reads and releases every batch. Operating days 310, held constant because it does not move the answer.
benefit_lines.conversion: AVOID-BACKFILL is arguable since Bethel carries four open roles, and we DECLINE to bank it for three reasons a CFO would raise first: a job posting is evidence of a posting not of an unfilled seat, we can't tell growth from turnover from seasonal cover, and at the conservative end 18 recovered minutes a day is not a fraction of an FTE anyone would act on. REDEPLOY is the realistic path. This converts to cash only on an explicit decision by the value owner.

benefit_lines.benefit: Avoided cost of committing to a multi-station rollout while two assumptions are unverified
benefit_lines.basis: ASSUMED, probability-weighted. Rework exposure 45,000 / 70,000 / 95,000 sized off the pilot's own build cost with reuse and a contact-capture allowance, never off a vendor figure. Fraction retired 0.40 / 0.55 / 0.70. events_per_year set so the model counts this ONE-TIME avoidance ONCE across the horizon and never annualizes it.
benefit_lines.precondition: Worth exactly ZERO unless a multi-station commitment is genuinely contemplated. If Bethel is the whole ambition, delete it. That precondition is the single biggest lever in the model and we put it on the table rather than bury it.

qualitative_quarantine: Storage-fee defensibility, real and argued, worth zero dollars in the formula because no number for disputed or unbilled storage at this company is sourceable.
Reduced billing-dispute friction, and its inverse risk.
Consignee experience in very small communities where the phone is the relationship.
The daily reconciliation gaining a downstream consumer, which tends to improve the count itself.
Option value of a clean consignee contact dataset, which every later notification idea rests on.
roi_analyst.phasing: Year one partial in every scenario. Six weeks to build then roughly ninety days of stabilization while the review habit forms and override rate settles. Year two full run rate at Bethel and nowhere else. NO compounding uplift modeled in year three, because claiming one at a station whose volumes we have never seen would stack a second invented number on the first. The one-time avoided-cost line is spread evenly by the script rather than landed at the readout where it really arrives, which makes computed payback LATER than reality, and that is the direction we want the error to lean.
roi_analyst.base_rate_note: MIT Project NANDA found about 95 percent of enterprise generative-AI pilots produce no measurable P&L impact, cause being the learning and integration gap rather than model quality, and the figure is directional with a debated denominator. RAND found more than 80 percent of AI projects fail, about twice the rate of non-AI IT, on five root causes led by misunderstanding the problem and lacking the data. Five reasons this build is designed for the small share that pays. ONE, and this is the main defence, it is barely an AI build at all, nothing a shipper reads is written by a model and the single conditional model node is DELETED if the reconciliation is an export. TWO, workflow-embedded, it rides a daily process that already exists so there is no new ritual to adopt and no vendor permission to obtain. THREE, adoption-owned, a named person who handled the freight releases the batch and override rate ships as a live metric. FOUR, measured, week one is baseline measurement before anything ships. FIVE, RAND's first two root causes are misunderstanding the problem and lacking the data, and those are precisely the two this phase exists to retire rather than assume away.
roi_analyst.value_owner: The operating number is owned by whoever holds the LEAD CARGO AGENT seat at Bethel, the role whose own posted spec already owns the daily on-hand reconciliation this desk rides. That seat is currently posted open, verified live today, so the owner must be named from existing Bethel staff on day one and handed over when the seat is filled, otherwise the number has no owner for the length of the pilot, which is how a case becomes fantasy by construction. Executive sponsor for anything beyond one hub is Lee Ryan, President.
roi_analyst.variance_check: Baseline measured in week one BEFORE anything ships, written down and signed off before a line of the desk is built. Four measures: minutes per operating day on arrival-status contact sampled across at least ten operating days, count of written notices issued against items newly on hand, notice-to-collection interval, and override rate once live. Re-measure at day 30, 60 and 90 against that baseline and report actual against the CONSERVATIVE drivers line by line, never against most-likely. THE FALSIFICATION TEST, stated up front so it can't be moved later: if measured arrival-status minutes at Bethel land below the conservative floor of one hour per operating day, the desk has NOT earned a network rollout and the readout says so in those words, whatever we have already been paid.

now.item: Publish the five missing policy pages, the freight cutoff time, the claims procedure, the embargo policy, perishables handling and station hours per location. No AI, no integration, no vendor, and we charge nothing.
now.metric: Five of five named policies live with an effective date printed on each. Countable the day it ships, no baseline needed, because the four absences are verified on a freight rules page read in full and station hours are absent site wide.
now.why_first: 16.2 on RICE against 2.08 for the paid pick, so cost of delay over size beats everything else on the board. Roughly half a week of THEIR effort, not ours. The caveat travels with it, half a week is the publishing effort and not the decision effort. It also unblocks two later items, an estimate can't say when freight moves until a cutoff exists, and a reference page can't answer what was never written down.

now.item: Open one support ticket with Takeflite asking whether the Bypass Mail Order lookup can be enabled on Ryan Air's tenant.
now.metric: A written yes or no from the vendor.
now.why_first: It costs one ticket and it can delete a four person-week build from the roadmap, so nothing on the board has a better ratio of what it might save to what it costs. If it is a tenant setting, nobody should be paid to build it, including us.

now.item: A measurement week at Bethel before anything is built. Take both baselines and answer the two unknowns in writing.
now.metric: Two baselines on file, both taken here because neither exists anywhere today. The two findings are yes or no answers on paper, not estimates.
now.why_first: No volume, call count or cycle time exists for this company anywhere, so every target after this is unfalsifiable without it. The two findings also decide the shape and the price of the build.

now.item: Arrival Notice Desk at Bethel, one hub, roughly six weeks, GATED on the measurement week.
now.metric: Share of arriving Bethel freight carrying a timestamped written notice within 24 hours, moving from the measured baseline toward 90 percent or better. Two guardrails outrank it: zero notices stating a wrong arrival or wrong storage start date, and override rate tracked live where a rate falling to zero is read as review becoming theatre. One honest cap stated up front, a once-daily trigger protects the RECORD better than it protects the PHONE, so a customer whose freight lands at ten in the morning may still call at noon.
now.why_first: The thinnest end-to-end slice that actually runs, riding a process the station is already required to run daily, so it needs no new integration and no vendor permission. Bethel because four of the ten open positions sit there, and because the on-hand list at Aniak and Nome plausibly mixes carriers.

next.item: Two-week access spike on Takeflite. Not a build and not priced as one.
next.metric: One dated document answering API access, event schema and contract terms with the decision written on it. Nobody prices the event engine before that answer exists.

next.item: Tariff Quote Engine, the published tariff turned into a calculator. ZERO AI, and that label is the point rather than an apology.
next.metric: Count of what-will-this-cost contacts against the measurement-week baseline. Every quote prints the rate table effective date so drift is visible. Honest flag that costs us work, sibling Northern Air Cargo already runs a self-serve estimator inside the same family, so reuse may beat a build from us.

next.item: Turn the bare Track Airbill hyperlink into a real tracking page with instructions and a subscribe control, carrying whatever the Takeflite ticket returned.
next.metric: Share of tracking sessions resolving without a follow-up call. Cross-carrier disclosure is pass or fail rather than a percentage, and one is a failure.

next.item: Second hub, chosen from stations whose on-hand reconciliation distinguishes carrier.
next.metric: Notice rate at the second hub reaching what Bethel actually measured, judged on that hub's own baseline. Aniak and Nome stay blocked until the reconciliation there separates Ryan Air freight from Everts freight, which is a finding to go and get, not an assumption to make.

later.item: A maintained internal reference page with search over the newly published policies, staff only. Rung one is a reference page, not a retrieval system.
later.metric: Share of logged agent questions answered from the page without asking a supervisor. Promotion trigger is explicit, log questions for a month after the policies publish, and if they show natural-language variety keyword search misses, the smarter version has earned its rung and gets built against an evaluation set drawn from those same logs.

later.item: Takeflite Event Notification Engine, moving only on a written yes from the access spike.
later.metric: Share of notices sent within an hour of arrival rather than at end of day. It carries a WORSE risk profile than the desk rather than a better one, since removing the station step removes the only person holding ground truth before a fee-starting message goes out, so any version keeps a human release step or it does not ship.

later.item: Open a freight account without a fax or a counter visit. All eight stations publish a fax number today.
later.metric: Share of new accounts opened without a fax or counter visit. Deliberately left fuzzy, it is the largest thing on the map and it touches billing and credit terms.

later.item: Document extraction on the flight and accounting paperwork stations prepare for Anchorage Accounting. The one place on the map where a model genuinely earns its keep.
later.metric: Rekeying minutes per station per week and correction rate. Both need a baseline that does not exist, and the only evidence today is a job spec rather than a stated complaint, so nobody scopes this until someone counts it.

later.item: A refund request form and a status page, so the chase call disappears.
later.metric: Share of refund requests submitted without a phone call, against a baseline that has to be counted first.

later.item: Assemble the evidence pack for a mishandled Priority shipment and hand it to a person. Software assembles, a human decides, and that split does not move.
later.metric: Time from claim raised to decision recorded. Judgment with money attached stays human, so the metric is never decisions made per hour.

later.item: An acknowledgement and routing rule on the charter request form.
later.metric: Share of charter requests acknowledged inside a stated window, once a window is stated.

delivery_lead.gates: Money is released one stage at a time and each stage is earned by the last stage's actuals. GATE ZERO COSTS NOTHING AT ALL. The five policy pages publish and the Takeflite ticket gets an answer, both Ryan Air's own work, and we bill for neither. GATE ONE releases the measurement week. GATE TWO releases the pilot build, and it clears only if the measurement week hands over both baselines plus the two findings in writing. If the reconciliation is a Takeflite export the extraction node is deleted from scope, the build gets cheaper and more reliable, and the ask comes down to match. If consignee contact details are missing, the work is repriced as contact capture before a line of the desk is built. GATE THREE sits at the end of the pilot and releases the second hub, clearing only if the notice rate rose from Bethel's own measured baseline to 90 percent or better, zero notices stated a wrong arrival or storage date, the override rate is not zero and somebody is reading it, and agent minutes moved in the right direction. If it does not clear, no second hub is funded and Ryan Air keeps the notice log, the templates, both baselines and both findings, which is a real off ramp and not a courtesy. GATE FOUR releases the Later lane. Two things are decisions already made rather than work deferred. The station voice and chat agent is killed and appears nowhere in any lane, and its cost of delay is genuinely negative so waiting improves it. Nothing in the dispatch or weather lane is ever built by us at any gate. NO CALENDAR DATE APPEARS ANYWHERE. Every duration is anchored to something Ryan Air controls, the pilot clock starts the day Bethel hands over a reconciliation sample and a consignee contact list, not on a date we picked.
